contract: Opt-in synchronous release of a binary credential snapshot for an exact bounded reference and scope under host-vouched current authority: one injected atomic resolver lookup, then one post-lookup Unix-ms expiry sample; redacted Credential with explicit reveal; malformed, unavailable, denied, missing and expired fixed failures. No store, process, cache, refresh or retry.
limits: Authority, scope meaning, coherent current-version lookup and time accuracy are consumer assumptions, not authentication or a transactional authorization guarantee.
Validity holds only at the expiry sample; revocation after lookup may still release the old snapshot. Previously returned bytes cannot be recalled.
Inspect is accidental-disclosure protection only; no encryption, memory erasure, sandbox, callback log redaction or global secrecy guarantee.
Callbacks execute synchronously and can block indefinitely; the consumer owns execution bounds.
Finite boundary and scheduled concurrency tests, not quantified proofs or provider revocation evidence.

grounding.claim: Exact schemas, bounds, refusal precedence, fixed failure classes, no callbacks on denial, redacted Inspect, catchable secret-bearing faults, post-lookup expiry and barrier-controlled coherent rotation/revocation schedules through the public API. Platform-only tests also run in a standalone copied consumer.
Elixir catch semantics for catchable errors, throws and exits; guards, function invocation and Inspect protocol dispatch. No hostile-VM isolation or uncatchable-kill handling.
OTP system time underlies the default Unix-millisecond clock; wall-clock accuracy and rollback behavior remain host assumptions.

The trusted host authenticates callers and supplies fresh exact authority, coherent atomic current-version resolver snapshots, accurate time and safe handling of revealed bytes. Callback side effects and external credential revocation are outside this boundary.

telemetry.contract: No events, logs, audit records, receipts or model context are emitted; the host owns instrumentation and callback safety.

config.contract: Per-call trusted resolver and optional clock selection, exact arities and keys validated before lookup; default clock is System.system_time(:millisecond). No global settings or hot-update API. Grant is authority data.

control.contract: No owned process, lifecycle or refresh/revocation command; the consumer owns the resolver and its updates.
